title: Provision-to-Ready: Validation Checklist (Draft)
content:
Context
- Sprint: Provision-to-ready automation (Dedicated capacity + fleet mgmt)
- This doc is the working validation checklist for the “Validating” readiness gate.
- Goal: nodes must pass these checks before control-plane marks Ready (and before node is admitted to serving pool).

Definitions / conventions
- “Pre-flight” = checks we run before kubelet join / before we mark node eligible for workloads. Some are image-time checks.
- “Post-flight” = checks after node is joined and has the validation agent running; includes runtime smoke + perf canary.
- Outputs:
  - Each check emits: status (pass/fail), duration, failure_reason (short string), artifact pointers (logs, bundle), and a recommended remediation.
  - Control plane stores the summary for UI + triage (see readiness service API notes).

Non-goals (for now)
- Not building a full benchmark suite.
- Not enforcing customer-specific performance SLOs at provisioning time. This is “minimum viability” readiness + catch obvious regressions.

Gate policy (WIP)
- Blocking vs Non-blocking:
  - Blocking failures keep node in Validating or move to Quarantined (depending on retry policy).
  - Non-blocking failures create a ticket + allow Ready (only if low risk). We should keep this list short.
- Retries:
  - Per-check retries + backoff handled by orchestrator/agent (ENG-4825). Some checks should be “no retry” (e.g., image/driver mismatch).


Checklist (Draft)

A) Pre-flight (image + boot) validations

A1. Image channel/version sanity
- What: confirm node is on expected golden image channel + version for the pool (candidate/stable pin).
- How:
  - Read expected image metadata from Terraform output / pool config.
  - Compare to node-reported image build id + channel label.
- Pass criteria:
  - Exact match on (channel, version) OR explicitly allowed “hotfix override” list.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking. Do not proceed; remediation is reimage or update pool pin (with audit event).
- Owner: Sahana Iyer (build pipeline) + Harish Reddy (ops policy)
- Notes/TODO:
  - Need canonical source of truth for “expected image”: control-plane pool config vs instance tags. Decide and document.

A2. Kernel + baseline node config
- What: validate baseline per node-configuration standard (kubelet flags, containerd config, sysctls, ulimits, time sync).
- How:
  - Agent runs a local config validator, compares to baseline policy bundle versioned with image.
- Pass criteria:
  - No “must-fix” deviations; warn-only for optional tunables.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking for must-fix deviations.
- Owner: Nina Petrova (baseline standard) + Gabe Wilson (agent integration)
- Notes:
  - Decide which settings are “must-fix” vs “warn”. (We’ve historically been too strict and created noise.)

A3. GPU hardware enumeration + basic health
- What: ensure GPUs present, expected SKU count, no obvious device errors.
- How:
  - nvidia-smi -L count == expected.
  - Check for persistent ECC errors (if supported) and recent Xid events.
- Pass criteria (initial proposal):
  - GPU count matches pool expectation.
  - No Xid in last 15 min.
  - ECC: 0 uncorrectable; correctable threshold TBD.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking. Retry once after driver reload; if still failing -> quarantine.
- Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (fleet) + Nina Petrova (thresholds)
- Open question:
  - What Xid codes are “instant quarantine” vs “retry”? Need list (ops-friendly).

A4. Driver/CUDA/NCCL parity
- What: ensure driver and userland toolkit match the expected matrix for that model + pool.
- How:
  - Read driver version from nvidia-smi.
  - Validate CUDA runtime version, NCCL version, OFED (if applicable).
- Pass criteria:
  - Versions match allowed set for the pool’s image build id.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking. No retry (reimage).
- Owner: Sahana Iyer (matrix) + Nina Petrova (compatibility)
- Notes:
  - We need to be careful about minor-version drift caused by unattended upgrades. Confirm we’re pinning.

A5. Disk layout + minimum free space
- What: verify disk mounts exist (ephemeral, docker/containerd, logs) and free space above minimum.
- How:
  - Check mount points; ensure containerd dir on intended volume.
- Pass criteria:
  - Mount points present.
  - Free space >= 20% (TBD) on key volumes.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking if mount missing; warn-only if low space but above hard minimum.
- Owner: Harish Reddy (ops) + Gabe Wilson
- TODO:
  - Confirm actual mount paths for each cloud + instance type.


B) Join + cluster prerequisites

B1. Kubelet joins cluster and becomes Ready (k8s perspective)
- What: ensure node can join the right cluster, node conditions healthy.
- How:
  - Watch for node registration, then verify node Ready=True.
- Pass criteria:
  - Ready=True within join timeout.
  - No repeated “NetworkUnavailable” or “DiskPressure” conditions.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking; retry join steps per orchestrator; quarantine if repeated.
- Owner: Gabe Wilson + Jordan Lee

B2. Validation agent DaemonSet healthy
- What: ensure validation agent pod scheduled and running (RBAC + tolerations correct).
- How:
  - Verify DS desired == available, agent reports heartbeat.
- Pass criteria:
  - Agent running within 5 min of node Ready.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking during rollout; may become non-blocking later if agent outage is global (needs policy).
- Owner: Gabe Wilson + Benji Okafor
- Notes:
  - This is a common “stuck in Validating” scenario; need clear error surfaces in UI.


C) Post-flight validations (blocking unless called out)

C1. GPU functional test (quick)
- What: run a minimal GPU compute test to catch obvious CUDA failures.
- How:
  - Run cuda-samples deviceQuery (or equivalent) inside standard runtime container.
- Pass criteria:
  - Exit 0; runtime within reasonable time.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking; retry once.
- Owner: Nina Petrova

C2. Network throughput + latency (node-level)
- What: ensure basic network performance isn’t obviously degraded.
- How:
  - Run iperf3 to a regional test endpoint (or node-to-node within cluster) + basic RTT check.
- Proposed thresholds (TBD by instance type):
  - RTT to regional endpoint < 2 ms (intra-AZ) / < 5 ms (intra-region)
  - Throughput > X Gbps sustained for 10–30s (needs per-SKU values)
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking during early rollouts; if too flaky, consider warn-only + quarantine only on extreme values.
- Owner: Keiko Yamamoto (guardrails) + Miles Thornton (SLO alignment)
- Open questions:
  - Where do we host the “network test endpoint” to avoid it being the bottleneck?
  - Should we test ENA config/offloads as part of baseline instead?

C3. Storage IOPS / disk warmup
- What: catch obvious EBS/volume attachment / perf anomalies.
- How:
  - fio quick profile (read/write) against the intended container/image cache volume.
- Proposed thresholds:
  - TBD by volume type. We likely set “floor” values to avoid false positives.
- Fail behavior:
  - Probably non-blocking initially unless volume misconfigured/missing.
- Owner: Harish Reddy + Miles Thornton
- Notes:
  - Past issue: first-run fio impacted caches and made later steps slow. Consider running a “warmup” only.

C4. NCCL fabric smoke test (multi-GPU)
- What: detect miswired/misconfigured GPU fabric (NVLink/PCIe) + interconnect issues early.
- How:
  - Run NCCL all-reduce or nccl-tests in a short job; single node multi-GPU at minimum.
  - Optional: add 2-node test later (deferred due to complexity).
- Proposed pass criteria:
  - Exit 0 within timeout.
  - Bandwidth above floor (per SKU) OR at least not catastrophically low.
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking; retry once with longer timeout; quarantine if persistent.
- Owner: Nina Petrova + Vanessa Ortiz
- Flake notes:
  - NCCL timeouts are known flaky under transient network jitter; need tuned backoff (ENG-4830).

C5. Runtime smoke test (inference engine)
- What: ensure we can run a minimal inference workload using the standard runtime container/entrypoint.
- How:
  - Pull runtime image, start server in test mode, run 1–3 short prompts, confirm tokens streamed.
- Pass criteria:
  - Server starts; no crashloop; inference returns 200 and output parseable.
  - Time to first token below a conservative ceiling (avoid strict perf gating here).
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking.
- Owner: Gabe Wilson + Ethan Park
- TODO:
  - Define which model to use for smoke test (tiny model to reduce load) vs using the real pool model.

C6. Post-provision perf canary (lightweight)
- What: run a “real” perf sanity check to catch regressions due to image/runtime changes.
- How:
  - perf-canary job: known prompt set, fixed concurrency, collect TTFT + tokens/sec.
- Proposed thresholds (initial placeholders; must be per GPU SKU + model):
  - TTFT p50 < 2.0s, p95 < 5.0s
  - Decode tokens/sec (aggregate) > floor value (TBD)
  - Error rate == 0 for canary run
- Fail behavior:
  - Blocking for severe regression; otherwise warn-only + ticket if borderline.
- Owner: Sergio Costa (canary wiring) + Allison Grant (metrics hygiene)
- Open question:
  - How do we avoid “canary creates load” when doing large scale bring-up? Maybe run per N nodes, not every node.

C7. Telemetry + audit signals present
- What: ensure we emit readiness events/metrics with correct tags (no high cardinality).
- How:
  - Check required metrics exist for the node/pool; verify trace spans created.
- Pass criteria:
  - Required metrics/spans present; tags conform to allowlist.
- Fail behavior:
  - Non-blocking by default (don’t block capacity for observability), but escalate if global break.
- Owner: Allison Grant + Aisha Bello
- Notes:
  - We should never tag per-node-id in metrics. Use pool_id/region/gpu_type/image_channel only.


D) Result mapping: readiness state + quarantine triggers (draft)

Recommended mapping
- Fail fast (no retry):
  - Image channel/version mismatch
  - Driver/CUDA/NCCL parity mismatch
- Retry then quarantine:
  - GPU health check fails after 1 retry
  - Kubelet join fails after max retries
  - NCCL smoke test fails after 1 retry
- Warn-only initially:
  - Storage IOPS borderline
  - Telemetry missing (unless global)

Quarantine: minimum info we need surfaced
- reason_code: e.g., GPU_XID_RECENT, DRIVER_MISMATCH, NCCL_TIMEOUT, JOIN_TIMEOUT
- short_summary: one sentence
- suggested_action: reimage | drain+rejoin | hardware_rma | investigate_network
- links: log bundle pointer, dashboard link


Open questions / TODOs (please add)
1) Thresholds by GPU type + model
- Need per-SKU floors for network + NCCL + perf canary.
- Owner: Nina Petrova + Miles Thornton

2) How strict is “network throughput” during early rollout?
- If too strict -> lots of quarantine -> capacity shortfall.
- Owner: Keiko Yamamoto + Vanessa Ortiz

3) Source of truth for expected image pin + pool config
- Terraform tags vs control plane config vs instance metadata.
- Owner: Jordan Lee + Sahana Iyer

4) Single-node vs multi-node NCCL
- Single-node catches many issues but not all (e.g., cross-node fabric).
- Owner: Nina Petrova

5) Artifact retention + PII/security
- What do we store from logs? Ensure we don’t capture secrets.
- Owner: Fiona McCarthy + Hanae Suzuki

6) Validation agent permissions (RBAC)
- Make sure we’re least-privilege; document required API calls.
- Owner: Fiona McCarthy + Benji Okafor

7) “Ready” definition across systems
- k8s Ready vs control-plane Ready vs serving-pool admission.
- Owner: Ethan Park + Benji Okafor


Notes from week 1 discussions (rough)
- Ordering: do cheap deterministic checks first (image/version, driver parity) before expensive tests.
- Make failures actionable: every check must have a remediation line, not just “failed”.
- Avoid alert noise: keep metric tags low-cardinality; use pool_id and image_channel.

Change log (informal)
- 2025-10-03: Initial draft created (Aisha)
- 2025-10-08: Added perf canary section + telemetry check; marked storage IOPS as likely warn-only
- 2025-10-18: Updated quarantine mapping; added security TODOs for artifact retention + RBAC
